problem: Learning-based multi-object search agents struggle with long horizons, especially in fine-grained continuous action spaces where end-to-end RL gets lost; waypoint-based hierarchies shorten the horizon but force a low control frequency and block joint control of other components.
motivation: Multi-object search in unmapped environments requires balancing long-term reasoning about where to go with short-term control and collision avoidance. Structured semantic maps offer universal features that could permit generalization from little data and small sim-to-real gap.
key_idea: Train a single RL policy on semantic maps that also predicts (as an auxiliary task and recursive input) the discretized direction to the next A* waypoint on the path to the closest target, using a curriculum mixing ground-truth and predicted directions.
insight: Explicit long-horizon intention prediction lets a flat continuous-control policy explore effectively: Map-only reaches 55.1% avg seen success versus 88.5% for the method, and directly predicting goal location helps only slightly (58.7%). Keeping gradient flow from the prediction head in prediction-only episodes is crucial; disabling it lowered prediction loss but caused a tremendous drop in success. The curriculum lets the policy learn to correct prediction errors instead of blindly following the ground truth.
method: Mapping module: projects 128x128 depth and semantic camera into a global top-down map with agent trace; extracts an egocentric coarse map (224x224, 6.6 cm) and a fine map (84x84, 3.3 cm); found objects are recolored
Encoders: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 for the coarse map (256-d), a 3-layer CNN for the fine map (128-d), concatenated into feature f_t

Predictive module: predicts a softmax over 12 angle bins to an A* waypoint 0.4-0.55 m along the shortest path to the closest target (map inflated by 0.2 m); trained with cross-entropy as an auxiliary loss and shared encoder
Recursive intention input: the policy sees previous predictions (as map overlay and in the robot state), prediction variances, collision flags, previous action and goal vector
Policy: PPO with 2-layer 64-unit MLP actor/critic and Gaussian policy over linear/angular velocity at 10 Hz; loss L = L_ppo + lambda*L_pred

Curriculum: episodes start with 16% chance of observing predictions (otherwise ground-truth direction), increased by 2% every 4 episodes after 50% success up to 72%; ground truth is never seen by the predictor
Real-world adaptations: map inflated by 5 cm, actions scaled by 0.55, softmax temperature 0.1

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 (ImageNet-pretrained) + small CNN + MLP, PPO policy trained with auxiliary prediction
setting.training_data: 8 iGibson challenge training apartments, about 4.5M environment steps, RL from scratch on semantic maps (ResNet-18 ImageNet-pretrained)
setting.observation: egocentric 128x128 depth + semantic camera aggregated into a global semantic top-down map, plus robot state and goal-object binary vector
setting.action_space: continuous linear and angular base velocities (LoCoBot differential drive, 10 Hz)
setting.privileged: Semantic camera (GT semantics) and assumed accurate pose/mapping; ground-truth path direction only during training; in real world a pre-annotated semantic map overlay with virtual objects

numbers.eval_set_note: 7 unseen apartments, 75 episodes each (525 episodes), 1-6 target objects

numbers_note: No standard benchmark; custom multi-object search in iGibson. Seen/unseen splits are per-object-count averages.
results: Average success 85.7% on unseen apartments vs 79.2% for the best baseline (reimplemented SGoLAM), and 88.5% on seen vs 65.3%. SGoLAM has slightly higher SPL on unseen (46.4 vs 43.9). Zero-shot real-world transfer succeeded in 22/40 episodes.
limitations: Relies on an accurate semantic camera and mapping; real-world tests use virtual objects on a pre-annotated semantic map
Real-world collisions (16 of 40 episodes) and oscillating predictions; SPL remains low and below SGoLAM on unseen scenes
Trained and evaluated on only iGibson apartments (8 train and 7 test scenes)
